historical_name: phenotypic exploration distribution Xi_sigma, and its three reported features
mathematical_object: probability distribution over the phenotype of one offspring of a fixed parent genotype, under the model's full mutation operator
estimator: Monte Carlo, 2000 independent offspring samples per individual per generation, computed for every member of the offspring population
reported_statistics: normalised pairwise mutual information matrix I'_ij = 2 I_ij / (H_i + H_j) over the 25 phenotypic variables
modular degree: summed probability that a variation at position i recurs at (i + 5k) mod 25, k = 1..4
unreported_statistic_found_in_recovered_: avgfit, the mean fitness of the sampled offspring, computed every generation by spectrum() in 02-stringRuleJTB/main.cpp and never plotted in any recovered publication
sampling_cost: 2000x the cost of the evolution it observes, at lambda=100 (see HC_T01_COMPUTE_MODEL.md)
what_it_sees: the shape of one-step phenotypic reachability from the current population, including correlation structure between phenotypic positions
what_it_misses: any notion of which reachable phenotypes are fitter, unless avgfit is used
its own estimator noise, which was never reported
substrate_dependence: the modular degree is hand-tailored to a period-5 target of length 25 and does not transfer; neutral degree and the mutual information matrix are substrate-general given a discrete phenotype with positions
causal_capability: none on its own; requires an intervention, which TOUSSAINT_ABLATION_SPEC.md supplies
known_confounds: the estimator is a function of the mutation operator, so any operator parameter moves it mechanically; see TRAP 1 in HC_T01_PREREGISTRATION.md
neutral degree is bounded and saturates, so its dynamic range shrinks as representations compact
no uncertainty was ever reported, so no historical noise floor exists to compare against
